import pytest
from sympy.physics.vector import dynamicsymbols, Point, ReferenceFrame, Vector
from sympy.physics.vector.point import _check_vector, _check_frame
from sympy import symbols


class TestPointInit:
    def test_point_init_basic(self):
        """Test basic Point initialization."""
        p = Point('P')
        assert p.name == 'P'
        assert p._pos_dict == {}
        assert p._vel_dict == {}
        assert p._acc_dict == {}

    def test_point_str_repr(self):
        """Test string representation of Point."""
        p = Point('MyPoint')
        assert str(p) == 'MyPoint'
        assert repr(p) == 'MyPoint'


class TestPointPosition:
    def test_set_pos_basic(self):
        """Test setting position between two points."""
        N = ReferenceFrame('N')
        p1 = Point('p1')
        p2 = Point('p2')
        p1.set_pos(p2, 10 * N.x)
        assert p1.pos_from(p2) == 10 * N.x

    def test_set_pos_zero_vector(self):
        """Test setting position with zero vector."""
        N = ReferenceFrame('N')
        p1 = Point('p1')
        p2 = Point('p2')
        p1.set_pos(p2, Vector(0))
        assert p1.pos_from(p2) == Vector(0)

    def test_set_pos_mutual(self):
        """Test that set_pos updates both points."""
        N = ReferenceFrame('N')
        p1 = Point('p1')
        p2 = Point('p2')
        p1.set_pos(p2, 10 * N.x)
        assert p2.pos_from(p1) == -10 * N.x

    def test_locatenew_basic(self):
        """Test creating new point with locatenew."""
        N = ReferenceFrame('N')
        P1 = Point('P1')
        P2 = P1.locatenew('P2', 10 * N.x)
        assert P2.name == 'P2'
        assert P1.pos_from(P2) == -10 * N.x

    def test_locatenew_invalid_name(self):
        """Test locatenew with invalid name type."""
        N = ReferenceFrame('N')
        P1 = Point('P1')
        with pytest.raises(TypeError):
            P1.locatenew(123, 10 * N.x)

    def test_locatenew_zero_value(self):
        """Test locatenew with zero value."""
        N = ReferenceFrame('N')
        P1 = Point('P1')
        P2 = P1.locatenew('P2', Vector(0))
        assert P1.pos_from(P2) == Vector(0)

    def test_pos_from_no_path(self):
        """Test pos_from when no path exists."""
        N = ReferenceFrame('N')
        p1 = Point('p1')
        p2 = Point('p2')
        # No position relationship established
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            p1.pos_from(p2)


class TestPointVelocity:
    def test_set_vel_basic(self):
        """Test setting velocity of a point."""
        N = ReferenceFrame('N')
        p1 = Point('p1')
        p1.set_vel(N, 10 * N.x)
        assert p1.vel(N) == 10 * N.x

    def test_vel_auto_calculation(self):
        """Test automatic velocity calculation from position."""
        N = ReferenceFrame('N')
        q = dynamicsymbols('q')
        p = Point('p')
        p.set_vel(N, 10 * N.x)
        p2 = Point('p2')
        p2.set_pos(p, q * N.x)
        result = p2.vel(N)
        assert result is not None

    def test_vel_not_defined(self):
        """Test vel when not defined and cannot be calculated."""
        N = ReferenceFrame('N')

    def test_set_vel_zero_vector(self):

        p1 = Point('p1')

        assert p1.vel(N) == Vector(0)

        N = ReferenceFrame('N')
        B = ReferenceFrame('B')

        O = Point('O')
        P = O.locatenew('P', dynamicsymbols('q') * B.x)

        O.set_vel(N, 0)
        result = P.v1pt_theory(O, N, B)

class TestPointComplexScenarios:
    def test_chain_of_points(self):
        """Test chain of multiple connected points."""
        N = ReferenceFrame('N')
        p1 = Point('p1')
        p2 = p1.locatenew('p2', 10 * N.x)
        p3 = p2.locatenew('p3', 5 * N.y)
        
        assert p1.pos_from(p2) == -10 * N.x
        assert p2.pos_from(p3) == -5 * N.y
        assert p1.pos_from(p3) == -10 * N.x - 5 * N.y

    def test_velocity_propagation(self):
        """Test velocity propagation through point chain."""
        N = ReferenceFrame('N')
        q = dynamicsymbols('q')
        p1 = Point('p1')
        p1.set_vel(N, 10 * N.x)
        p2 = p1.locatenew('p2', q * N.x)
        
        # p2's velocity should include p1's velocity plus derivative of position
        v2 = p2.vel(N)
        assert v2 is not None

    def test_acceleration_propagation(self):
        """Test acceleration propagation through point chain."""
        N = ReferenceFrame('N')
        q = dynamicsymbols('q')
        p1 = Point('p1')
        p1.set_acc(N, 5 * N.x)
        p2 = p1.locatenew('p2', q * N.x)
        
        # p2's acceleration should include p1's acceleration
        a2 = p2.acc(N)
        assert a2 is not None

    def test_multiple_frames_velocity(self):
        """Test velocity in multiple reference frames."""
        N = ReferenceFrame('N')
        B = ReferenceFrame('B')
        p = Point('p')
        p.set_vel(N, 10 * N.x)
        p.set_vel(B, 5 * B.x)
        
        assert p.vel(N) == 10 * N.x
        assert p.vel(B) == 5 * B.x

    def test_symbols_as_points(self):
        """Test creating Points using symbols."""
        N = ReferenceFrame('N')
        u1, u2 = dynamicsymbols('u1 u2')
        A, B = symbols('A B', cls=Point)
        
        assert isinstance(A, Point)
        assert isinstance(B, Point)
        
        A.set_vel(N, u1 * N.x + u2 * N.y)
        B.set_vel(N, u2 * N.x + u1 * N.y)
        
        diff = A.acc(N) - B.acc(N)
        assert diff is not None

class TestRegisterMethod(TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.site = AdminSite(name='test_admin')
        self.factory = RequestFactory()
    
    def test_register_single_model(self):
        """Test registering a single model"""
        model = MagicMock(spec=ModelBase)
        model._meta.abstract = False
        model._meta.swapped = False
        model.__name__ = 'TestModel'
        
        self.site.register(model)
        
        self.assertTrue(self.site.is_registered(model))
    
    def test_register_multiple_models_as_iterable(self):
        """Test registering multiple models as iterable"""
        model1 = MagicMock(spec=ModelBase)
        model1._meta.abstract = False
        model1._meta.swapped = False
        model1.__name__ = 'Model1'
        
        model2 = MagicMock(spec=ModelBase)
        model2._meta.abstract = False
        model2._meta.swapped = False
        model2.__name__ = 'Model2'
        
        self.site.register([model1, model2])
        
        self.assertTrue(self.site.is_registered(model1))
        self.assertTrue(self.site.is_registered(model2))
    
    def test_register_abstract_model_raises_improperly_configured(self):
        """Test registering an abstract model raises ImproperlyConfigured"""
        model = MagicMock(spec=ModelBase)
        model._meta.abstract = True
        model.__name__ = 'AbstractModel'
        
        with self.assertRaises(ImproperlyConfigured):
            self.site.register(model)
    
    def test_register_already_registered_raises_already_registered(self):
        """Test registering an already registered model raises AlreadyRegistered"""
        model = MagicMock(spec=ModelBase)
        model._meta.abstract = False
        model._meta.swapped = False
        model.__name__ = 'TestModel'
        
        self.site.register(model)
        
        with self.assertRaises(AlreadyRegistered):
            self.site.register(model)
    
    def test_register_with_custom_admin_class(self):
        """Test registering with custom admin class"""
        model = MagicMock(spec=ModelBase)
        model._meta.abstract = False
        model._meta.swapped = False
        model.__name__ = 'TestModel'
        
        custom_admin = MagicMock(spec=ModelAdmin)
        
        self.site.register(model, custom_admin)
        
        self.assertTrue(self.site.is_registered(model))
    
    def test_register_with_options_creates_dynamic_class(self):
        """Test register with keyword options creates dynamic admin class"""
        model = MagicMock(spec=ModelBase)
        model._meta.abstract = False
        model._meta.swapped = False
        model.__name__ = 'TestModel'
        
        self.site.register(model, list_display=['field1'])
        
        self.assertTrue(self.site.is_registered(model))
    
    def test_register_swapped_model_ignored(self):
        """Test registering a swapped model is ignored"""
        model = MagicMock(spec=ModelBase)
        model._meta.abstract = False
        model._meta.swapped = True
        model.__name__ = 'SwappedModel'
        
        self.site.register(model)
        
        self.assertFalse(self.site.is_registered(model))


class TestUnregisterMethod(TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.site = AdminSite(name='test_admin')
        self.factory = RequestFactory()
    
    def test_unregister_single_model(self):
        """Test unregistering a single model"""
        model = MagicMock(spec=ModelBase)
        model._meta.abstract = False
        model._meta.swapped = False
        model.__name__ = 'TestModel'
        
        self.site.register(model)
        self.assertTrue(self.site.is_registered(model))
        
        self.site.unregister(model)
        self.assertFalse(self.site.is_registered(model))
    
    def test_unregister_multiple_models_as_iterable(self):
        """Test unregistering multiple models as iterable"""
        model1 = MagicMock(spec=ModelBase)
        model1._meta.abstract = False
        model1._meta.swapped = False
        model1.__name__ = 'Model1'
        
        model2 = MagicMock(spec=ModelBase)
        model2._meta.abstract = False
        model2._meta.swapped = False
        model2.__name__ = 'Model2'
        
        self.site.register([model1, model2])
        self.site.unregister([model1, model2])
        
        self.assertFalse(self.site.is_registered(model1))
        self.assertFalse(self.site.is_registered(model2))
    
    def test_unregister_not_registered_raises_not_registered(self):
        """Test unregistering an unregistered model raises NotRegistered"""
        model = MagicMock(spec=ModelBase)
        model._meta.abstract = False
        model.__name__ = 'TestModel'
        
        with self.assertRaises(NotRegistered):
            self.site.unregister(model)

class TestPermissionAndViews(TestCase):

    def test_has_permission_active_staff(self):
        """Test has_permission returns True for active staff user"""

        request.user.is_active = True
        request.user.is_staff = True
        
        self.assertTrue(self.site.has_permission(request))

        request.user = MagicMock()
        request.user.is_active = False
        request.user.is_staff = True
        
        self.assertFalse(self.site.has_permission(request))

        request = self.factory.get('/admin/')
        request.user = MagicMock()
        request.user.is_active = True
        request.user.is_staff = False
        
        self.assertFalse(self.site.has_permission(request))

        request.META['SCRIPT_NAME'] = ''
        request.user = MagicMock()

        request.user.is_staff = True

        request.user = MagicMock()
        request.user.is_active = True
        request.user.is_staff = True

class TestModelBase(TestCase):
    """Tests for ModelBase metaclass."""

    def setUp(self):
        # Create a simple test model dynamically
        from django.db.models.base import ModelBase
        
        self.TestModel = type(
            'TestModel',
            (models.Model,),
            {
                '__module__': __name__,
                'Meta': type('Meta', (), {'app_label': 'test'}),
            }
        )
    
    def test_modelbase_new_with_parents(self):
        """Test ModelBase.__new__ with parent classes."""
        # Verify that ModelBase properly creates new model classes
        self.assertTrue(hasattr(self.TestModel, '_meta'))
        self.assertTrue(hasattr(self.TestModel, 'objects'))
    
    def test_modelbase_add_to_class(self):
        """Test ModelBase.add_to_class method."""
        class TestClass:
            pass
        
        TestClass._meta = mock.MagicMock()
        
        def contribute_to_class(cls, name):
            setattr(cls, name, 'contributed')
        
        value = mock.MagicMock()
        value.contribute_to_class = contribute_to_class
        
        TestClass.add_to_class = lambda cls, name, val: contribute_to_class(val, name)
        TestClass.add_to_class('test_field', value)
        
        self.assertTrue(hasattr(TestClass, 'test_field'))
    
    def test_subclass_exception(self):
        """Test subclass_exception function."""
        from django.db.models.base import subclass_exception
        
        class Parent:
            pass
        
        ExceptionClass = subclass_exception(
            'CustomException',
            (Parent,),
            __name__,
            attached_to=Parent
        )
        
        self.assertEqual(ExceptionClass.__module__, __name__)
        self.assertIn('Parent.CustomException', ExceptionClass.__qualname__)
        
        # Test pickling
        pickled = pickle.dumps(ExceptionClass)
        unpickled = pickle.loads(pickled)
        self.assertEqual(unpickled, ExceptionClass)


class TestModelInit(TestCase):
    """Tests for Model.__init__ method."""

    def setUp(self):
        class TestModel(models.Model):
            name = models.CharField(max_length=100)
            age = models.IntegerField(default=0)
            
            class Meta:
                app_label = 'test'
        
        self.TestModel = TestModel
    
    def test_init_with_args(self):
        """Test Model initialization with positional arguments."""
        instance = self.TestModel('John', 25)
        self.assertEqual(instance.name, 'John')
        self.assertEqual(instance.age, 25)
    
    def test_init_with_kwargs(self):
        """Test Model initialization with keyword arguments."""
        instance = self.TestModel(name='Jane', age=30)
        self.assertEqual(instance.name, 'Jane')
        self.assertEqual(instance.age, 30)
    
    def test_init_with_args_exceeding_fields(self):
        """Test Model initialization raises IndexError when args exceed fields."""
        with self.assertRaises(IndexError):
            self.TestModel('John', 25, 'extra_arg')
    
    def test_init_deferred_values(self):
        """Test Model initialization with DEFERRED values."""
        from django.db.models.base import DEFERRED
        
        instance = self.TestModel(DEFERRED, DEFERRED)
        self.assertIsNone(instance.name)
        self.assertEqual(instance.age, 0)
    
    def test_post_init_signal(self):
        """Test that post_init signal is sent during initialization."""
        signal_received = []
        
        def handler(sender, instance, **kwargs):
            signal_received.append(instance)
        
        post_init.connect(handler)
        
        try:
            instance = self.TestModel(name='Test', age=20)
            self.assertEqual(len(signal_received), 1)
            self.assertEqual(signal_received[0], instance)
        finally:
            post_init.disconnect(handler)

class TestModelPickle(TestCase):

        new_instance.__setstate__(state)
        
        self.assertEqual(new_instance.name, instance.name)

class TestAssertAllFinite:
    def test_assert_all_finite_valid(self):
        """Test that valid finite arrays pass."""
        X = np.array([1.0, 2.0, 3.0])
        assert_all_finite(X)
    
    def test_assert_all_finite_nan_raises(self):
        """Test that NaN values raise ValueError."""
        X = np.array([1.0, np.nan, 3.0])
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="NaN"):
            assert_all_finite(X)
    
    def test_assert_all_finite_inf_raises(self):
        """Test that infinity values raise ValueError."""
        X = np.array([1.0, np.inf, 3.0])
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="infinity"):
            assert_all_finite(X)
    
    def test_assert_all_finite_allow_nan(self):
        """Test allow_nan parameter."""
        X = np.array([1.0, np.nan, 3.0])
        assert_all_finite(X, allow_nan=True)
    
    def test_assert_all_finite_sparse(self):
        """Test with sparse matrix."""
        X = sp.csr_matrix([[1.0, 2.0], [3.0, 4.0]])
        assert_all_finite(X)
    
    def test_assert_all_finite_sparse_nan_raises(self):
        """Test sparse matrix with NaN raises error."""
        X = sp.csr_matrix([[1.0, np.nan], [3.0, 4.0]])
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="NaN"):
            assert_all_finite(X)


class TestAsFloatArray:
    def test_as_float_array_basic(self):
        """Test basic conversion to float array."""
        X = np.array([1, 2, 3])
        result = as_float_array(X)
        assert result.dtype in [np.float32, np.float64]
    
    def test_as_float_array_copy_false(self):
        """Test copy=False behavior."""
        X = np.array([1.0, 2.0, 3.0], dtype=np.float64)
        result = as_float_array(X, copy=False)
        # May or may not be same object depending on implementation
        assert result.dtype == np.float64
    
    def test_as_float_array_copy_true(self):
        """Test copy=True creates new array."""
        X = np.array([1.0, 2.0, 3.0], dtype=np.float64)
        result = as_float_array(X, copy=True)
        assert result is not X
    
    def test_as_float_array_sparse(self):
        """Test with sparse matrix."""
        X = sp.csr_matrix([[1.0, 2.0], [3.0, 4.0]])
        result = as_float_array(X)
        assert sp.issparse(result)
    
    def test_as_float_array_force_all_finite(self):
        """Test force_all_finite parameter."""
        X = np.array([1.0, 2.0, 3.0])
        result = as_float_array(X, force_all_finite=True)
        assert result.dtype in [np.float32, np.float64]

"""Unit tests for sklearn/utils/_pprint.py"""

import io
from collections import OrderedDict
from unittest.mock import Mock, patch

import pytest

from sklearn.utils._pprint import (
    _EstimatorPrettyPrinter,
    KeyValTuple,
    KeyValTupleParam,
    _changed_params,
    _safe_repr,
)
from sklearn.base import BaseEstimator


class SimpleEstimator(BaseEstimator):
    """Simple estimator for testing purposes."""

    def __init__(self, param1=1, param2="default", param3=None):
        self.param1 = param1
        self.param2 = param2
        self.param3 = param3


class AnotherEstimator(BaseEstimator):
    """Another estimator for testing."""

    def __init__(self, a=10, b=20, c=30):
        self.a = a
        self.b = b
        self.c = c


class LongParamsEstimator(BaseEstimator):
    """Estimator with many parameters for testing ellipsis behavior."""

    def __init__(self, p1=1, p2=2, p3=3, p4=4, p5=5, p6=6, p7=7, p8=8, p9=9, p10=10):
        self.p1 = p1
        self.p2 = p2
        self.p3 = p3
        self.p4 = p4
        self.p5 = p5
        self.p6 = p6
        self.p7 = p7
        self.p8 = p8
        self.p9 = p9
        self.p10 = p10


def test_changed_params_basic():
    """Test _changed_params returns only non-default parameters."""
    est = SimpleEstimator(param1=5, param2="custom")
    params = _changed_params(est)
    assert "param1" in params
    assert "param2" in params
    assert "param3" not in params  # default value


def test_changed_params_all_defaults():
    """Test _changed_params when all params are defaults."""
    est = SimpleEstimator()
    params = _changed_params(est)
    assert len(params) == 0


def test_changed_params_with_nan():
    """Test _changed_params handles NaN values correctly."""
    from sklearn.utils import is_scalar_nan
    
    class NanEstimator(BaseEstimator):
        def __init__(self, val=float('nan')):
            self.val = val
    
    est = NanEstimator(val=float('nan'))
    params = _changed_params(est)
    # NaN should not be considered changed if both are NaN
    assert len(params) == 0

class TestCheckSolver:

        """Test that valid solvers are accepted"""
        for solver in ['liblinear', 'newton-cg', 'lbfgs', 'sag', 'saga']:
            for penalty in ['l1', 'l2', 'elasticnet', 'none']:
                try:

                except ValueError:
                    # Some combinations are invalid
                    pass

        """Test that invalid solver raises error"""
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Logistic Regression supports only solvers"):
            _check_solver('invalid_solver', 'l2', False)
    
    def test_invalid_penalty(self):

    def test_solver_penalty_combination(self):
        """Test that incompatible solver-penalty combinations raise error"""
        # newton-cg doesn't support l1
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="supports only 'l2' or 'none' penalties"):
            _check_solver('newton-cg', 'l1', False)

import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch, call

from django.template import autoreload
from django.template.backends.django import DjangoTemplates
from django.utils._os import to_path


class GetTemplateDirectoriesTests(unittest.TestCase):
    @patch('django.template.autoreload.engines')
    @patch('django.template.autoreload.Path')
    def test_get_template_directories_with_django_backend(self, mock_path_class, mock_engines):
        """Test get_template_directories returns directories from DjangoTemplates backend"""
        # Setup mock
        mock_cwd = MagicMock(spec=Path)
        mock_path_class.cwd.return_value = mock_cwd
        
        mock_backend = MagicMock(spec=DjangoTemplates)
        mock_engine = MagicMock()
        mock_engine.dirs = ['/templates', '/static/templates']
        mock_loader = MagicMock()
        mock_loader.get_dirs.return_value = ['/loader/templates']
        mock_engine.template_loaders = [mock_loader]
        
        mock_backend.engine = mock_engine
        mock_engines.all.return_value = [mock_backend]
        
        # Call function
        result = autoreload.get_template_directories()
        
        # Verify results
        self.assertIsInstance(result, set)
        self.assertEqual(len(result), 3)
        
        # Verify cwd was called
        mock_path_class.cwd.assert_called_once()
    
    @patch('django.template.autoreload.engines')
    @patch('django.template.autoreload.Path')
    def test_get_template_directories_filters_non_django_backends(self, mock_path_class, mock_engines):
        """Test non-DjangoTemplates backends are skipped"""
        mock_cwd = MagicMock(spec=Path)
        mock_path_class.cwd.return_value = mock_cwd
        
        mock_other_backend = MagicMock()
        mock_django_backend = MagicMock(spec=DjangoTemplates)
        mock_engine = MagicMock()
        mock_engine.dirs = []
        mock_django_backend.engine = mock_engine
        
        mock_engines.all.return_value = [mock_other_backend, mock_django_backend]

        """Test is_django_path filtering works"""

class TestProtectedError(TestCase):

"""
Unit tests for UnitSystem class in sympy.physics.units.unitsystem
"""

import pytest
from sympy import S, Mul, Pow, Add, Derivative, Function
from sympy.core.symbol import symbols
from sympy.physics.units import Quantity, meter, second, kilogram, ampere, kelvin, mole, candela
from sympy.physics.units.definitions.dimension_definitions import (
    Dimension, charge, length, time, temperature, pressure, energy, mass
)
from sympy.physics.units.systems.si import dimsys_SI, SI
from sympy.physics.units.quantities import Quantity as Q


class TestUnitSystemInit:
    """Tests for UnitSystem initialization"""

    def test_init_with_base_units(self):
        """Test initialization with base units"""
        from sympy.physics.units.unitsystem import UnitSystem
        
        base = [meter, second]
        system = UnitSystem(base, name="test")
        
        assert system.name == "test"
        assert system._base_units == tuple(base)
        assert len(system._base_units) == 2

    def test_init_with_units(self):
        """Test initialization with additional units"""
        from sympy.physics.units.unitsystem import UnitSystem
        
        base = [meter, second]
        units = [kilogram]
        system = UnitSystem(base, units=units, name="extended")
        
        assert system.name == "extended"
        assert kilogram in system._units

    def test_init_with_derived_units(self):
        """Test initialization with derived units"""
        from sympy.physics.units.unitsystem import UnitSystem
        
        base = [meter, second]
        derived = {length: Quantity("velocity")}
        system = UnitSystem(base, derived_units=derived, name="with_derived")
        
        assert system.derived_units == derived

    def test_init_registers_in_unit_systems(self):
        """Test that unit system is registered in _unit_systems dict"""
        from sympy.physics.units.unitsystem import UnitSystem
        
        base = [meter, second]
        system = UnitSystem(base, name="reg_test")
        
        assert "reg_test" in UnitSystem._unit_systems
        assert UnitSystem._unit_systems["reg_test"] is system


class TestUnitSystemStrRepr:
    """Tests for string and repr representations"""

    def test_str_with_name(self):
        """Test __str__ returns name when set"""
        from sympy.physics.units.unitsystem import UnitSystem
        
        base = [meter, second]
        system = UnitSystem(base, name="my_system")
        
        assert str(system) == "my_system"

class TestModelBase(TestCase):
    """Tests for the ModelBase metaclass."""

    def test_subclass_exception_creation(self):
        """Test that subclass_exception creates proper exception classes."""
        class FakeAttachedTo:
            __qualname__ = 'FakeAttachedTo'

        ExceptionClass = subclass_exception(
            'TestException',
            (ValueError,),
            'test_module',
            attached_to=FakeAttachedTo
        )

        self.assertEqual(ExceptionClass.__module__, 'test_module')
        self.assertIn('TestException', ExceptionClass.__qualname__)
        
        # Should be picklable
        pickled = pickle.dumps(ExceptionClass)
        unpickled = pickle.loads(pickled)
        self.assertEqual(unpickled, ExceptionClass)

    def test_has_contribute_to_class(self):
        """Test _has_contribute_to_class function."""
        from django.db.models.base import _has_contribute_to_class
        
        class HasContribute:
            def contribute_to_class(self, cls, name):
                pass
        
        class NoContribute:
            pass
        
        self.assertTrue(_has_contribute_to_class(HasContribute()))
        self.assertFalse(_has_contribute_to_class(NoContribute))
        self.assertFalse(_has_contribute_to_class(int))

class TestModelValidation(TestCase):
    """Tests for model validation methods."""

    def setUp(self):
        class TestModel(Model):
            id = AutoField(primary_key=True)
            name = CharField(max_length=100, unique=True)
            email = CharField(max_length=100, blank=True)
            age = IntegerField()
            
            class Meta:
                app_label = 'test_app'
                unique_together = [('name', 'email')]
        
        self.TestModel = TestModel

    def test_clean_method(self):
        """Test clean method can be overridden."""
        class CustomModel(TestModel):
            def clean(self):
                if self.age < 0:
                    raise ValidationError({'age': 'Age must be positive'})
        
        instance = CustomModel(age=-1)
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            instance.clean()

    def test_clean_fields(self):
        """Test clean_fields method."""
        instance = self.TestModel(name='test', email='', age=25)
        instance.clean_fields()
        self.assertEqual(instance.email, '')

    def test_validate_unique_no_errors(self):
        """Test validate_unique when no errors occur."""
        instance = self.TestModel(name='unique_name', email='test@example.com', age=25)
        instance.validate_unique()  # Should not raise

    def test_validate_unique_with_error(self):
        """Test validate_unique raises error on duplicate."""
        instance1 = self.TestModel(name='duplicate', email='dup@example.com', age=25)
        instance1.save()
        
        instance2 = self.TestModel(name='duplicate', email='dup@example.com', age=30)
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            instance2.validate_unique()

    def test_full_clean(self):
        """Test full_clean method."""
        instance = self.TestModel(name='valid', email='valid@example.com', age=25)
        instance.full_clean()  # Should not raise

    def test_full_clean_with_validation_error(self):
        """Test full_clean raises ValidationError."""
        instance = self.TestModel(name='invalid', email='invalid@example.com', age=-1)
        instance.full_clean()  # Should not raise by default

    def test_clean_fields_exclude(self):
        """Test clean_fields with exclude parameter."""
        instance = self.TestModel(name='test', email='', age=25)
        instance.clean_fields(exclude=['email'])  # Should skip email validation


class TestModelSave(TestCase):
    """Tests for model save methods."""

    def setUp(self):

            value = IntegerField(default=0)

    def test_save_new_instance(self):
        """Test saving a new instance."""
        instance = self.TestModel(name='test', value=10)
        instance.save()
        self.assertIsNotNone(instance.id)
        self.assertFalse(instance._state.adding)

    def test_save_existing_instance(self):
        """Test saving an existing instance."""
        instance = self.TestModel(name='test', value=10)
        instance.save()
        original_id = instance.id
        instance.name = 'updated'
        instance.save()
        self.assertEqual(instance.id, original_id)

    def test_save_force_insert(self):
        """Test save with force_insert."""
        instance = self.TestModel(name='test', value=10)
        instance.save(force_insert=True)
        self.assertIsNotNone(instance.id)

    def test_save_update_fields(self):
        """Test save with update_fields."""
        instance = self.TestModel(name='test', value=10)
        instance.save()
        instance.name = 'updated'
        instance.value = 20
        instance.save(update_fields=['name'])
        
        # Reload to verify only name was updated
        refreshed = self.TestModel.objects.get(pk=instance.pk)
        self.assertEqual(refreshed.name, 'updated')
        self.assertEqual(refreshed.value, 10)

    def test_save_invalid_update_fields(self):
        """Test save with invalid update_fields."""
        instance = self.TestModel(name='test', value=10)
        instance.save()
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            instance.save(update_fields=['nonexistent_field'])

    def test_save_base_signals(self):
        """Test save_base sends signals."""
        received_pre_save = []
        received_post_save = []
        
        def pre_save_handler(sender, **kwargs):
            received_pre_save.append(kwargs)
        
        def post_save_handler(sender, **kwargs):
            received_post_save.append(kwargs)
        
        from django.db.models.signals import pre_save, post_save
        pre_save.connect(pre_save_handler, sender=self.TestModel)
        post_save.connect(post_save_handler, sender=self.TestModel)
        
        try:
            instance = self.TestModel(name='test', value=10)
            instance.save()
            self.assertEqual(len(received_pre_save), 1)
            self.assertEqual(len(received_post_save), 1)
        finally:
            pre_save.disconnect(pre_save_handler, sender=self.TestModel)
            post_save.disconnect(post_save_handler, sender=self.TestModel)

    def test_save_base_raw(self):
        """Test save_base with raw=True."""
        instance = self.TestModel(name='test', value=10)
        instance.save_base(raw=True)
        self.assertIsNotNone(instance.id)

# coding: utf-8
"""
Unit tests for NeighborhoodComponentsAnalysis
"""

import numpy as np
from numpy.testing import assert_array_almost_equal, assert_array_equal
import pytest
from scipy.optimize import minimize

from sklearn.neighbors.nca import NeighborhoodComponentsAnalysis
from sklearn.datasets import load_iris, make_classification
from sklearn.exceptions import ConvergenceWarning
from sklearn.utils.validation import check_is_fitted


class TestNeighborhoodComponentsAnalysis:
    """Test suite for NeighborhoodComponentsAnalysis"""

    @pytest.fixture
    def iris_data(self):
        """Load iris dataset for testing"""
        return load_iris(return_X_y=True)

    @pytest.fixture
    def simple_data(self):
        """Create simple 2D classification data"""
        X = np.array([[0, 0], [1, 1], [2, 2], [3, 3]])
        y = np.array([0, 0, 1, 1])
        return X, y

    @pytest.fixture
    def nca_instance(self):
        """Create default NCA instance"""
        return NeighborhoodComponentsAnalysis(random_state=42)

    def test_init_default_parameters(self):
        """Test default parameter initialization"""
        nca = NeighborhoodComponentsAnalysis()
        assert nca.n_components is None
        assert nca.init == 'auto'
        assert nca.warm_start is False
        assert nca.max_iter == 50
        assert nca.tol == 1e-5
        assert nca.callback is None
        assert nca.verbose == 0
        assert nca.random_state is None

    def test_init_custom_parameters(self):
        """Test custom parameter initialization"""
        nca = NeighborhoodComponentsAnalysis(
            n_components=2,
            init='random',
            warm_start=True,
            max_iter=100,
            tol=1e-3,
            verbose=1,
            random_state=123
        )
        assert nca.n_components == 2
        assert nca.init == 'random'
        assert nca.warm_start is True
        assert nca.max_iter == 100
        assert nca.tol == 1e-3
        assert nca.verbose == 1
        assert nca.random_state == 123

    def test_fit_basic(self, iris_data, nca_instance):
        """Test basic fit functionality"""
        X, y = iris_data
        nca = nca_instance.fit(X, y)
        assert hasattr(nca, 'components_')
        assert hasattr(nca, 'n_iter_')
        assert isinstance(nca.components_, np.ndarray)
        assert nca.components_.shape[1] == X.shape[1]

    def test_transform_after_fit(self, iris_data, nca_instance):
        """Test transform after fitting"""
        X, y = iris_data
        nca = nca_instance.fit(X, y)
        X_transformed = nca.transform(X)
        assert X_transformed.shape[0] == X.shape[0]
        if nca.n_components is None:
            assert X_transformed.shape[1] == X.shape[1]
        else:
            assert X_transformed.shape[1] == nca.n_components

    def test_not_fitted_error(self, nca_instance):
        """Test NotFittedError when transform called before fit"""
        X = np.array([[1, 2], [3, 4]])
        with pytest.raises(Exception):  # NotFittedError
            nca_instance.transform(X)

    def test_n_components_validation(self, nca_instance):
        """Test n_components validation"""
        X = np.array([[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]])
        y = np.array([0, 1])
        
        # Valid n_components
        nca = NeighborhoodComponentsAnalysis(n_components=2)
        nca.fit(X, y)
        
        # Invalid n_components (greater than features)
        nca_invalid = NeighborhoodComponentsAnalysis(n_components=5)
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            nca_invalid.fit(X, y)

    def test_max_iter_validation(self, nca_instance):
        """Test max_iter validation"""
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            NeighborhoodComponentsAnalysis(max_iter=0).fit(
                np.array([[1, 2]]), np.array([0])
            )

    def test_tol_validation(self, nca_instance):
        """Test tol validation"""
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            NeighborhoodComponentsAnalysis(tol=-1).fit(
                np.array([[1, 2]]), np.array([0])
            )

    def test_verbose_output(self, iris_data, capsys):
        """Test verbose output during fit"""
        X, y = iris_data
        nca = NeighborhoodComponentsAnalysis(verbose=1)
        nca.fit(X, y)
        captured = capsys.readouterr()
        assert 'NCA' in captured.out or 'Training took' in captured.out

    def test_callback_functionality(self, iris_data):
        """Test callback function during optimization"""
        X, y = iris_data
        callback_calls = []
        
        def callback(transformation, n_iter):
            callback_calls.append((transformation.copy(), n_iter))
        
        nca = NeighborhoodComponentsAnalysis(callback=callback, max_iter=5)
        nca.fit(X, y)
        
        assert len(callback_calls) > 0
        assert all(isinstance(call[0], np.ndarray) for call in callback_calls)

    def test_warm_start(self, iris_data):
        """Test warm_start functionality"""
        X, y = iris_data
        
        # First fit
        nca1 = NeighborhoodComponentsAnalysis(warm_start=False, random_state=42)
        nca1.fit(X, y)
        components_first = nca1.components_.copy()
        
        # Second fit with warm_start
        nca2 = NeighborhoodComponentsAnalysis(warm_start=True, random_state=42)
        nca2.fit(X, y)
        
        # Components should be similar due to warm_start
        assert np.allclose(nca1.components_, nca2.components_)

    def test_warm_start_dimension_mismatch(self, iris_data):
        """Test warm_start raises error on dimension mismatch"""
        X1, y1 = iris_data
        X2, y2 = iris_data
        X2 = X2[:, :2]  # Different number of features
        
        nca = NeighborhoodComponentsAnalysis(warm_start=True)
        nca.fit(X1, y1)
        
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            nca.fit(X2, y2)

    def test_init_auto_selection(self, iris_data):
        """Test auto initialization selection"""
        X, y = iris_data
        nca = NeighborhoodComponentsAnalysis(init='auto', random_state=42)
        nca.fit(X, y)
        assert hasattr(nca, 'components_')

    def test_init_pca(self, iris_data):
        """Test PCA initialization"""
        X, y = iris_data
        nca = NeighborhoodComponentsAnalysis(init='pca', random_state=42)
        nca.fit(X, y)
        assert hasattr(nca, 'components_')

    def test_init_identity(self, iris_data):
        """Test identity initialization"""
        X, y = iris_data
        nca = NeighborhoodComponentsAnalysis(init='identity', random_state=42)
        nca.fit(X, y)
        assert hasattr(nca, 'components_')

    def test_init_random(self, iris_data):
        """Test random initialization"""
        X, y = iris_data
        nca = NeighborhoodComponentsAnalysis(init='random', random_state=42)
        nca.fit(X, y)
        assert hasattr(nca, 'components_')

    def test_init_lda(self, iris_data):
        """Test LDA initialization"""
        X, y = iris_data
        nca = NeighborhoodComponentsAnalysis(init='lda', random_state=42)
        nca.fit(X, y)
        assert hasattr(nca, 'components_')

    def test_init_numpy_array(self, iris_data):
        """Test numpy array initialization"""
        X, y = iris_data
        n_features = X.shape[1]
        init_matrix = np.eye(n_features)
        
        nca = NeighborhoodComponentsAnalysis(init=init_matrix, random_state=42)
        nca.fit(X, y)
        assert hasattr(nca, 'components_')

    def test_init_invalid_value(self):
        """Test invalid init value raises error"""
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            NeighborhoodComponentsAnalysis(init='invalid').fit(
                np.array([[1, 2]]), np.array([0])
            )

    def test_init_array_shape_mismatch(self):
        """Test init array shape mismatch raises error"""
        X = np.array([[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]])
        y = np.array([0, 1])
        init_matrix = np.eye(2)  # Wrong shape
        
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            NeighborhoodComponentsAnalysis(init=init_matrix).fit(X, y)

    def test_init_array_output_greater_than_input(self):
        """Test init array with output > input raises error"""
        X = np.array([[1, 2], [3, 4]])
        y = np.array([0, 1])
        init_matrix = np.eye(3, 2)  # Output dim > input dim
        
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            NeighborhoodComponentsAnalysis(init=init_matrix).fit(X, y)

    def test_init_array_n_components_mismatch(self):
        """Test init array with n_components mismatch raises error"""
        X = np.array([[1, 2], [3, 4]])
        y = np.array([0, 1])
        init_matrix = np.eye(2, 2)
        
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            NeighborhoodComponentsAnalysis(
                n_components=1, init=init_matrix
            ).fit(X, y)

    def test_callback_not_callable(self):
        """Test non-callable callback raises error"""
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            NeighborhoodComponentsAnalysis(callback="not callable").fit(
                np.array([[1, 2]]), np.array([0])
            )

    def test_convergence_warning(self, simple_data):
        """Test convergence warning when algorithm doesn't converge"""
        X, y = simple_data
        nca = NeighborhoodComponentsAnalysis(max_iter=1, tol=1e-10, verbose=0)
        
        with pytest.warns(ConvergenceWarning):
            nca.fit(X, y)

    def test_components_shape(self, iris_data):
        """Test components shape matches expected dimensions"""
        X, y = iris_data
        nca = NeighborhoodComponentsAnalysis(n_components=2, random_state=42)
        nca.fit(X, y)
        
        assert nca.components_.shape == (2, X.shape[1])

    def test_transform_new_data(self, iris_data):
        """Test transform on new data"""
        X, y = iris_data
        nca = NeighborhoodComponentsAnalysis(random_state=42)
        nca.fit(X, y)

        """Test basic expression evaluation"""
        d = {"x": 5}

        assert result == 8

        """Test evaluation with built-in functions"""
        d = {"os": os, "sys": sys, "platform": platform}
        result = compiled_eval("len('hello')", d)
        assert result == 5

        """Test evaluation with config object"""
        mock_config = MagicMock()

        assert result is None

    def test_compiled_eval_with_platform(self):
        """Test evaluation using platform module"""
        d = {"platform": platform}
        result = compiled_eval("platform.system()", d)

class TestColorbarBasic:
    """Test basic Colorbar functionality."""
    
    def setup_method(self):
        """Set up test fixtures."""
        self.fig, self.ax = plt.subplots()
        
    def teardown_method(self):
        """Clean up after tests."""
        plt.close('all')
    
    def test_colorbar_creation(self):
        """Test basic colorbar creation with mappable."""
        im = self.ax.imshow(np.random.rand(10, 10))
        cbar = self.fig.colorbar(im, ax=self.ax)
        assert isinstance(cbar, Colorbar)
        assert cbar.ax is not None
    
    def test_colorbar_vertical_orientation(self):
        """Test vertical colorbar orientation."""
        im = self.ax.imshow(np.random.rand(10, 10))
        cbar = self.fig.colorbar(im, ax=self.ax, orientation='vertical')
        assert cbar.orientation == 'vertical'
    
    def test_colorbar_horizontal_orientation(self):
        """Test horizontal colorbar orientation."""
        im = self.ax.imshow(np.random.rand(10, 10))
        cbar = self.fig.colorbar(im, ax=self.ax, orientation='horizontal')
        assert cbar.orientation == 'horizontal'
    
    def test_colorbar_with_cmap_norm(self):
        """Test colorbar creation with cmap and norm instead of mappable."""
        cbar = Colorbar(self.ax, cmap=cm.viridis, norm=Normalize())
        assert cbar.cmap is not None
        assert cbar.norm is not None
    
    def test_colorbar_remove(self):
        """Test removing colorbar."""
        im = self.ax.imshow(np.random.rand(10, 10))
        cbar = self.fig.colorbar(im, ax=self.ax)
        cbar.remove()
        # After removal, the colorbar's ax should be removed

class TestColoredLevelFormatter:
    """Tests for ColoredLevelFormatter class."""

    def test_init_with_format(self):
        """Test initialization with log format."""
        terminalwriter = MagicMock()
        formatter = ColoredLevelFormatter(terminalwriter, DEFAULT_LOG_FORMAT)
        assert formatter._fmt == DEFAULT_LOG_FORMAT

    def test_init_without_levelname_fmt(self):
        """Test initialization when format doesn't contain %(levelname)."""
        terminalwriter = MagicMock()
        formatter = ColoredLevelFormatter(terminalwriter, "%(message)s")
        assert formatter._original_fmt == "%(message)s"

    def test_format_with_color(self):
        """Test format method applies colorization."""
        terminalwriter = MagicMock()
        terminalwriter.markup.return_value = "[RED]INFO[RESET]"

        formatter = ColoredLevelFormatter(
            terminalwriter,
            "%(levelname)-8s %(message)s"
        )

        record = logging.LogRecord(
            name="test",
            level=logging.INFO,
            pathname="",
            lineno=0,
            msg="test message",
            args=(),
            exc_info=None
        )

        result = formatter.format(record)
        assert "INFO" in result

    def test_colored_level_formatter_regex(self):
        """Test LEVELNAME_FMT_REGEX matching."""
        match = ColoredLevelFormatter.LEVELNAME_FMT_REGEX.search("%(levelname)-8s")
        assert match is not None
        assert match.group() == "%(levelname)-8s"

        match = ColoredLevelFormatter.LEVELNAME_FMT_REGEX.search("%(message)s")
        assert match is None

    def test_colored_level_formatter_all_levels(self):
        """Test ColoredLevelFormatter handles all log levels."""
        terminalwriter = MagicMock()
        terminalwriter.markup.return_value = "MARKUP"

        formatter = ColoredLevelFormatter(
            terminalwriter,
            "%(levelname)-8s %(message)s"
        )

        for level in [logging.CRITICAL, logging.ERROR, logging.WARNING,
                      logging.INFO, logging.DEBUG, logging.NOTSET]:
            record = logging.LogRecord(
                name="test",
                level=level,
                pathname="",
                lineno=0,
                msg="test",
                args=(),
                exc_info=None
            )
            formatter.format(record)
            if level != logging.NOTSET:
                assert level in formatter._level_to_fmt_mapping


class TestCatchingLogs:
    """Tests for catching_logs context manager."""

    def test_catching_logs_basic(self):
        """Test basic usage of catching_logs."""
        handler = logging.StreamHandler()
        with catching_logs(handler):
            pass

        root_logger = logging.getLogger()
        assert handler not in root_logger.handlers

    def test_catching_logs_with_formatter(self):
        """Test catching_logs with custom formatter."""
        handler = logging.StreamHandler()
        formatter = logging.Formatter("%(message)s")

        with catching_logs(handler, formatter=formatter):
            pass

        assert handler.formatter == formatter

    def test_catching_logs_with_level(self):
        """Test catching_logs with level setting."""
        handler = logging.StreamHandler()

        with catching_logs(handler, level=logging.DEBUG):
            pass

        root_logger = logging.getLogger()
        assert root_logger.level <= logging.DEBUG

    def test_catching_logs_preserves_original_level(self):
        """Test that original logger level is restored."""
        original_level = logging.getLogger().level
        handler = logging.StreamHandler()

        with catching_logs(handler, level=logging.DEBUG):
            pass

        assert logging.getLogger().level == original_level

    def test_catching_logs_double_handler(self):
        """Test catching_logs doesn't add duplicate handlers."""
        handler = logging.StreamHandler()
        root_logger = logging.getLogger()
        root_logger.addHandler(handler)

        try:
            with catching_logs(handler):
                pass

            assert root_logger.handlers.count(handler) == 1
        finally:
            root_logger.removeHandler(handler)

    def test_catching_logs_with_exception(self):
        """Test catching_logs works with exceptions."""
        handler = logging.StreamHandler()

        try:
            with catching_logs(handler):
                raise ValueError("test exception")
        except ValueError:
            pass

        root_logger = logging.getLogger()
        assert handler not in root_logger.handlers

def test_find():
    from sympy.geometry.util import find
    
    x = Symbol('x')
    eq = x**2 + 2*x + 1
    assert find(x, eq) == x
    
    # Test ValueError when symbol not found
    y = Symbol('y')
    raises(ValueError, lambda: find(y, eq))
    
    # Test ambiguous case with multiple occurrences
    z = Symbol('z')
    eq2 = z**2 + z
    raises(ValueError, lambda: find(z, eq2))

    from sympy.geometry.point import Point3D

from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from unittest.mock import patch, MagicMock

from django.conf import settings
from django.test import TestCase, override_settings
from django.contrib.auth.models import User
from django.contrib.auth.tokens import PasswordResetTokenGenerator


class PasswordResetTokenGeneratorTests(TestCase):
    """Tests for PasswordResetTokenGenerator class."""

    def setUp(self):
        self.generator = PasswordResetTokenGenerator()
        self.user = User.objects.create_user(
            username='testuser',
            password='testpass',
            email='test@example.com'
        )

    def test_init_uses_secret_key(self):
        """Test that __init__ uses SECRET_KEY if not provided."""
        generator = PasswordResetTokenGenerator()
        self.assertEqual(generator.secret, settings.SECRET_KEY)

    def test_init_uses_default_hashing_algorithm(self):
        """Test that __init__ uses DEFAULT_HASHING_ALGORITHM if not provided."""
        generator = PasswordResetTokenGenerator()
        self.assertIsNotNone(generator.algorithm)

    @override_settings(DEFAULT_HASHING_ALGORITHM='sha256')
    def test_init_custom_algorithm(self):
        """Test that __init__ respects custom algorithm setting."""
        generator = PasswordResetTokenGenerator()
        self.assertEqual(generator.algorithm, 'sha256')

    @patch('django.contrib.auth.tokens.PasswordResetTokenGenerator._now')
    def test_make_token_returns_string(self, mock_now):
        """Test that make_token returns a string token."""
        mock_now.return_value = datetime.now()
        token = self.generator.make_token(self.user)
        self.assertIsInstance(token, str)
        self.assertIn('-', token)
        parts = token.split('-')
        self.assertEqual(len(parts), 2)

    @patch('django.contrib.auth.tokens.PasswordResetTokenGenerator._now')
    def test_make_token_unique_for_different_users(self, mock_now):
        """Test that make_token produces different tokens for different users."""
        mock_now.return_value = datetime.now()
        user2 = User.objects.create_user(
            username='testuser2',
            password='testpass2',
            email='test2@example.com'
        )
        token1 = self.generator.make_token(self.user)
        token2 = self.generator.make_token(user2)
        self.assertNotEqual(token1, token2)

    @patch('django.contrib.auth.tokens.PasswordResetTokenGenerator._now')
    def test_check_token_valid_token(self, mock_now):
        """Test check_token with a valid token."""
        mock_now.return_value = datetime.now()
        token = self.generator.make_token(self.user)
        result = self.generator.check_token(self.user, token)
        self.assertTrue(result)

    @patch('django.contrib.auth.tokens.PasswordResetTokenGenerator._now')
    def test_check_token_invalid_token_format(self, mock_now):
        """Test check_token with invalid token format."""
        mock_now.return_value = datetime.now()
        result = self.generator.check_token(self.user, 'invalid-token-format')
        self.assertFalse(result)

    @patch('django.contrib.auth.tokens.PasswordResetTokenGenerator._now')
    def test_check_token_empty_token(self, mock_now):

    def test_check_token_expired_token(self, mock_now):

        token = self.generator.make_token(self.user)

            mock_now_after.return_value = future_time

        self.assertEqual(result, 0)

        dt_later = datetime(2001, 1, 2)
        result_later = self.generator._num_seconds(dt_later)
        self.assertEqual(result_later, 86400)  # 24 hours in seconds

        """Test check_token handles missing dash in token."""
        token = "nodash"
        result = self.generator.check_token(self.user, token)
        self.assertFalse(result)

    def test_check_token_multiple_dashes(self):
        """Test check_token handles multiple dashes in token."""
        token = "part1-part2-part3"
        result = self.generator.check_token(self.user, token)
        self.assertFalse(result)

    def test_make_token_consistent_for_same_user_and_time(self):
        """Test that make_token is consistent for same user and timestamp."""
        with patch.object(self.generator, '_now') as mock_now:

            token1 = self.generator.make_token(self.user)
            token2 = self.generator.make_token(self.user)
            self.assertEqual(token1, token2)

    def test_make_token_changes_when_password_changes(self):
        """Test that token changes when user password changes."""
        with patch.object(self.generator, '_now') as mock_now:

        """Test that token changes when user last_login changes."""
        with patch.object(self.generator, '_now') as mock_now:

            token1 = self.generator.make_token(self.user)

class TestResolverMatch(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.func = lambda request: None
        self.args = [1, 2]
        self.kwargs = {'key': 'value'}
        self.url_name = 'test_url'
        self.app_names = ['app1', 'app2']
        self.namespaces = ['ns1', 'ns2']
        self.route = '/test/'
        self.tried = []

    def test_init_basic(self):
        match = ResolverMatch(
            self.func, self.args, self.kwargs,
            url_name=self.url_name,
            app_names=self.app_names,
            namespaces=self.namespaces,
            route=self.route,
            tried=self.tried
        )
        self.assertEqual(match.func, self.func)
        self.assertEqual(match.args, self.args)
        self.assertEqual(match.kwargs, self.kwargs)
        self.assertEqual(match.url_name, self.url_name)
        self.assertEqual(match.route, self.route)
        self.assertEqual(match.tried, self.tried)
        self.assertEqual(match.app_names, self.app_names)
        self.assertEqual(match.app_name, 'app1:app2')
        self.assertEqual(match.namespaces, self.namespaces)
        self.assertEqual(match.namespace, 'ns1:ns2')

    def test_init_empty_app_names(self):
        match = ResolverMatch(
            self.func, self.args, self.kwargs,
            url_name=None,
            app_names=[],
            namespaces=[]
        )
        self.assertEqual(match.app_names, [])
        self.assertEqual(match.app_name, '')
        self.assertEqual(match.namespaces, [])
        self.assertEqual(match.namespace, '')

    def test_init_class_based_view(self):
        class ViewClass:
            pass
        
        view_instance = ViewClass()
        match = ResolverMatch(
            view_instance, self.args, self.kwargs,
            url_name=None,
            app_names=None,
            namespaces=None
        )
        self.assertIn('ViewClass', match._func_path)

    def test_getitem(self):
        match = ResolverMatch(
            self.func, self.args, self.kwargs,
            url_name=self.url_name
        )
        self.assertEqual(match[0], self.func)
        self.assertEqual(match[1], self.args)
        self.assertEqual(match[2], self.kwargs)

    def test_repr_with_function(self):
        match = ResolverMatch(
            self.func, self.args, self.kwargs,
            url_name=self.url_name
        )
        repr_str = repr(match)
        self.assertIn('ResolverMatch', repr_str)
        self.assertIn('args=%r' % self.args, repr_str)
        self.assertIn('kwargs=%r' % self.kwargs, repr_str)

    def test_repr_with_partial(self):
        partial_func = functools.partial(self.func)
        match = ResolverMatch(
            partial_func, self.args, self.kwargs,
            url_name=self.url_name
        )
        repr_str = repr(match)
        self.assertIn('partial', repr_str)


class TestRegexPattern(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.pattern = RegexPattern(r'^test/(?P<pk>[0-9]+)/$')

    def test_init(self):
        self.assertEqual(self.pattern._regex, r'^test/(?P<pk>[0-9]+)/$')
        self.assertIsNotNone(self.pattern.name)
        self.assertFalse(self.pattern._is_endpoint)

    def test_match_success(self):
        result = self.pattern.match('/test/123/')
        self.assertIsNotNone(result)
        new_path, args, kwargs = result
        self.assertEqual(new_path, '')
        self.assertEqual(args, ())
        self.assertEqual(kwargs, {'pk': '123'})

    def test_match_failure(self):
        result = self.pattern.match('/other/path/')
        self.assertIsNone(result)

    def test_match_without_named_groups(self):
        pattern = RegexPattern(r'^test/\d+/$')
        result = pattern.match('/test/123/')
        self.assertIsNotNone(result)
        new_path, args, kwargs = result
        self.assertEqual(args, ('123',))
        self.assertEqual(kwargs, {})

    def test_check_pattern_startswith_slash(self):
        # When APPEND_SLASH=True (default), this should warn
        pattern = RegexPattern(r'^/test/$')
        warnings = pattern._check_pattern_startswith_slash()
        if settings.APPEND_SLASH:
            self.assertTrue(len(warnings) > 0)
        else:
            self.assertEqual(len(warnings), 0)

    def test_check_include_trailing_dollar(self):
        pattern = RegexPattern(r'^test/$')
        warnings = pattern._check_include_trailing_dollar()
        self.assertEqual(len(warnings), 0)

    def test_compile_invalid_regex(self):
        with self.assertRaises(Exception):
            RegexPattern(r'[invalid(regex')._compile(r'[invalid(regex')

    def test_str_representation(self):
        self.assertEqual(str(self.pattern), r'^test/(?P<pk>[0-9]+)/$')

    """Integration tests for URL resolution"""

        self.pattern = RegexPattern(r'^api/')
        self.test_pattern = RegexPattern(r'^test/$')
        self.test_url_pattern = URLPattern(self.test_pattern, self.callback, name='test')
        
        self.resolver = URLResolver(
            self.pattern,
            [self.test_url_pattern],
            namespace='api',
            app_name='api'
        )

    def test_full_resolution_chain(self):
        result = self.resolver.resolve('/api/test/')
        self.assertIsNotNone(result)
        self.assertEqual(result.func, self.callback)
        self.assertEqual(result.url_name, 'test')
        self.assertIn('api', result.namespace)

    def test_resolution_with_args(self):
        pattern = RegexPattern(r'^api/(?P<pk>[0-9]+)/$')
        url_pattern = URLPattern(pattern, self.callback, name='detail')
        
        resolver = URLResolver(
            RegexPattern(r'^api/'),
            [url_pattern],
            namespace='api',
            app_name='api'
        )
        
        result = resolver.resolve('/api/123/')
        self.assertIsNotNone(result)
        self.assertEqual(result.kwargs['pk'], '123')

    def test_resolution_with_kwargs(self):
        pattern = RegexPattern(r'^api/(?P<name>[a-z]+)/$')
        url_pattern = URLPattern(pattern, self.callback, name='user')
        
        resolver = URLResolver(
            RegexPattern(r'^api/'),
            [url_pattern],
            namespace='api',
            app_name='api'
        )
        
        result = resolver.resolve('/api/john/')
        self.assertIsNotNone(result)
        self.assertEqual(result.kwargs['name'], 'john')

    def test_nested_resolvers(self):
        inner_pattern = RegexPattern(r'^inner/$')
        inner_url_pattern = URLPattern(inner_pattern, self.callback, name='inner')
        
        inner_resolver = URLResolver(
            RegexPattern(r'^inner/'),
            [inner_url_pattern],
            namespace='inner',
            app_name='inner'
        )

        outer_url_pattern = URLPattern(outer_pattern, inner_resolver, name='outer')
        
        resolver = URLResolver(
            RegexPattern(r'^'),
            [outer_url_pattern],
            namespace='root',
            app_name='root'
        )
        
        result = resolver.resolve('/outer/inner/')
        self.assertIsNotNone(result)

            self.resolver.resolve('/api/nonexistent/')

            app_name='api'
        )
        
        result = resolver.resolve('/api/test/')
        self.assertIsNotNone(result)

import unittest
from unittest import mock

from django.core.exceptions import FieldError, ImproperlyConfigured, ValidationError
from django.db import models
from django.forms import (
    BooleanField, CharField, Form, IntegerField, ModelChoiceField,
    ModelMultipleChoiceField, MultipleChoiceField,
)
from django.forms.models import (
    ALL_FIELDS, BaseModelForm, BaseModelFormSet, BaseInlineFormSet,
    ModelChoiceIterator, ModelChoiceIteratorValue, ModelChoiceField,
    ModelForm, ModelFormOptions, ModelMultipleChoiceField, construct_instance,
    fields_for_model, inlineformset_factory, modelform_factory,
    modelform_defines_fields, model_to_dict, modelformset_factory,
)


class TestModel(models.Model):
    name = models.CharField(max_length=100)
    age = models.IntegerField()
    email = models.EmailField()
    is_active = models.BooleanField(default=True)
    
    class Meta:
        app_label = 'test_app'


class TestModelWithFK(models.Model):
    name = models.CharField(max_length=100)
    parent = models.ForeignKey(TestModel, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    
    class Meta:
        app_label = 'test_app'


class TestModelWithM2M(models.Model):
    name = models.CharField(max_length=100)
    tags = models.ManyToManyField('TestModel', related_name='related_tags')
    
    class Meta:
        app_label = 'test_app'


class TestConstructInstance(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.instance = TestModel(name='Test', age=25, email='test@example.com')
        
    def test_construct_instance_basic(self):
        """Test basic instance construction from form data."""
        form_data = {
            'name': 'Updated Name',
            'age': 30,
            'email': 'updated@example.com',
            'is_active': True,
        }
        
        # Create a simple form-like object
        class MockForm:
            cleaned_data = form_data
            
        result = construct_instance(MockForm(), self.instance)
        self.assertEqual(result.name, 'Updated Name')
        self.assertEqual(result.age, 30)
        self.assertEqual(result.email, 'updated@example.com')
        self.assertEqual(result.is_active, True)
        
    def test_construct_instance_with_exclude(self):
        """Test instance construction with excluded fields."""

)

class TestRefineMain:
    """Tests for the main refine function"""
    
    def test_refine_basic_atom(self):
        """Test refine with basic atoms"""
        assert refine(x, Q.real(x)) == x
        assert refine(S(5), Q.real(x)) == S(5)
    
    def test_refine_sqrt_positive(self):
        """Test refine with sqrt and positive assumption"""
        assert refine(sqrt(x**2), Q.positive(x)) == x
    
    def test_refine_sqrt_real(self):
        """Test refine with sqrt and real assumption"""
        result = refine(sqrt(x**2), Q.real(x))
        assert isinstance(result, Abs)
    
    def test_refine_boolean_true(self):
        """Test refine with boolean expressions that evaluate to True"""
        assert refine(Q.real(x), Q.positive(x)) is True
    
    def test_refine_boolean_unchanged(self):
        """Test refine with boolean expressions that cannot be determined"""
        result = refine(Q.positive(x), Q.real(x))
        assert result == Q.positive(x)
    
    def test_refine_non_basic_expr(self):
        """Test refine with non-Basic expressions"""
        assert refine("string", Q.real(x)) == "string"
        assert refine(5, Q.real(x)) == 5

    def test_refine_abs_positive(self):
        """Test refine_abs with positive argument"""
        from sympy.assumptions.refine import refine_abs
        assert refine_abs(Abs(x), Q.positive(x)) == x
    
    def test_refine_abs_negative(self):
        """Test refine_abs with negative argument"""
        from sympy.assumptions.refine import refine_abs
        assert refine_abs(Abs(x), Q.negative(x)) == -x
    
    def test_refine_abs_nonnegative(self):
        """Test refine_abs with non-negative argument"""
        from sympy.assumptions.refine import refine_abs
        result = refine_abs(Abs(x), Q.real(x) & ~Q.negative(x))
        assert result == x
    
    def test_refine_abs_mul(self):
        """Test refine_abs with multiplication"""
        from sympy.assumptions.refine import refine_abs
        result = refine_abs(Abs(x*y), Q.positive(x) & Q.positive(y))
        assert result == x * y

        from sympy.assumptions.refine import refine_atan2

class PrepopulatedFieldsJsTests(TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.context = Context({})

    def test_prepopulated_fields_js_with_adminform(self):
        mock_field = Mock()
        mock_field.auto_id = "id_name"
        mock_field.name = "name"
        mock_field.field.max_length = 100
        mock_field.field.allow_unicode = True

        mock_dependency = Mock()
        mock_dependency.auto_id = "id_dep"
        mock_dependency.name = "dep_name"

        mock_prepopulated_field = {
            "field": mock_field,
            "dependencies": [mock_dependency]
        }

class SubmitRowTests(TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.context = {
            "add": True,
            "change": False,
            "is_popup": False,
            "save_as": False,
            "show_save": True,
            "show_save_and_add_another": True,
            "show_save_and_continue": True,
            "has_add_permission": True,
            "has_change_permission": False,
            "has_view_permission": False,
            "has_editable_inline_admin_formsets": False,
            "has_delete_permission": False,
            "show_delete": True,
        }

    def test_submit_row_basic(self):
        result = submit_row(Context(self.context))

        self.assertIn("can_change", result)
        self.assertIn("show_delete_link", result)
        self.assertIn("show_save_as_new", result)
        self.assertIn("show_save_and_add_another", result)
        self.assertIn("show_save_and_continue", result)
        self.assertIn("show_save", result)
        self.assertIn("show_close", result)

    def test_submit_row_with_change_permission(self):
        context = self.context.copy()
        context["change"] = True
        context["has_change_permission"] = True

        result = submit_row(Context(context))

        self.assertTrue(result["can_change"])
        self.assertFalse(result["show_close"])

    def test_submit_row_with_is_popup(self):
        context = self.context.copy()
        context["is_popup"] = True

        result = submit_row(Context(context))

        self.assertFalse(result["show_save_as_new"])
        self.assertFalse(result["show_save_and_continue"])

    def test_submit_row_with_save_as(self):
        context = self.context.copy()
        context["save_as"] = True
        context["change"] = True
        context["has_add_permission"] = True

        result = submit_row(Context(context))

        self.assertTrue(result["show_save_as_new"])

    def test_submit_row_with_editable_inline_admin_formsets(self):
        context = self.context.copy()
        context["has_editable_inline_admin_formsets"] = True

        result = submit_row(Context(context))

        self.assertTrue(result["can_change"])

    def test_submit_row_default_values(self):
        context = {
            "add": True,
            "change": False,
            "is_popup": False,
            "save_as": False,
            "has_add_permission": True,
            "has_change_permission": False,
            "has_view_permission": False,
            "has_editable_inline_admin_formsets": False,
            "has_delete_permission": False,
        }

        result = submit_row(Context(context))

        self.assertTrue(result["show_save"])
        self.assertTrue(result["show_save_and_add_another"])
        self.assertFalse(result["show_save_and_continue"])

    def test_submit_row_show_save_false(self):
        context = self.context.copy()
        context["show_save"] = False

        result = submit_row(Context(context))

        self.assertFalse(result["show_save"])
        self.assertTrue(result["show_close"])

    def test_submit_row_has_delete_permission(self):
        context = self.context.copy()
        context["change"] = True
        context["has_delete_permission"] = True

        result = submit_row(Context(context))

        self.assertTrue(result["show_delete_link"])

class TestBinXmlEscape:
    def test_escape_basic(self):
        result = bin_xml_escape("hello world")
        assert "hello" in str(result)
        
    def test_escape_less_than(self):
        result = bin_xml_escape("<test>")
        assert "#" in str(result)
        
    def test_escape_greater_than(self):
        result = bin_xml_escape(">test<")
        assert "#" in str(result)
        
    def test_escape_ampersand(self):
        result = bin_xml_escape("a&b")
        assert "#" in str(result)
        
    def test_escape_quotes(self):
        result = bin_xml_escape('"test"')
        assert "#" in str(result)
        
    def test_escape_newline(self):
        result = bin_xml_escape("line1\nline2")
        assert "line1" in str(result)
        
    def test_escape_unicode(self):
        result = bin_xml_escape("\u00E9\u00E8")  # éè
        assert isinstance(str(result), str)


class TestMangleTestAddress:
    def test_simple_path(self):
        result = mangle_test_address("test_file.py::test_func")
        assert result == ["test_file", "test_func"]
        
    def test_with_params(self):
        result = mangle_test_address("test_file.py::test_func[param]")
        assert result == ["test_file", "test_func[param]"]
        
    def test_nested_classes(self):
        result = mangle_test_address("test_file.py::TestClass::test_method")
        assert result == ["test_file", "TestClass", "test_method"]
        
    def test_remove_empty_params(self):
        result = mangle_test_address("test_file.py::()::test_func")
        assert "()" not in result
        
    def test_with_separators(self):
        result = mangle_test_address("path/to/test_file.py::TestClass::test_method")
        assert "path.to.test_file" in result[0]

    def test_session_finish_calculates_numtests(self):
        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False) as f:
            tmpfile = f.name
        try:
            logxml = LogXML(tmpfile, None)
            logxml.stats["passed"] = 5
            logxml.stats["failure"] = 2
            logxml.stats["skipped"] = 1
            logxml.stats["error"] = 1
            logxml.cnt_double_fail_tests = 0
            numtests = (

                + logxml.stats["skipped"]

            )
